text:
jess: FYI the weekly KPI digest just flagged a 35% drop in MQLs from paid channels vs last week. dashboard: https://app.redwood/marketing/kpis
maya: I see the same on the conversion tile — top-of-funnel sessions steady, landing conversion down.
liam: quick check: some ad variants were updated yesterday with new URLs. could be UTM fragmentation.
omar: pulled forms logs: small spike in 400s around 09:40 UTC, but not enough to explain whole delta.
anne: I rolled a rewrite rule to consolidate old /launch page to /launch-2026 earlier today; might have stripped query params for certain user agents.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-04-18T09:35 by anne 14 web-redirects v4.2 14 no rollback.
jess: ok let's do a quick triage: liam 12 normalize UTMs estimate; maya 12 GA4 vs HS crosswalk last 7d; omar 12 count form errors; anne 12 confirm redirect behavior and preserve-params patch. reconvene in 30.
liam: running a mapping script now 12 early result: remapping `utm_campaign=launch_april` and `launch-april` -> +145 attributed leads.
maya: GA4 filter change was not the cause; crosswalk shows ~-160 HS creates vs baseline.
omar: form errors = 28 between 09:36-09:44 UTC, mostly 400 bad request from malformed payloads (likely bot hits).
anne: I pushed preserve-params flag at 09:52 and validated param passthrough in staging; will promote if green.
jess: combined numbers suggest UTM fragmentation + redirect params explained ~170-180 of the drop. still ~15% unexplained; could be ad creative CTR differences.
liam: recommend adding automatic UTM normalization in ETL and a dashboard alert for sudden attribution shift.
maya: I'll add a visualization for campaign-level retention and drop it in the marketing channel.
anne: will open a tiny postmortem and note the rollback checklist in case redirects cause similar issues.
jess: thanks team 12 keep updates in this thread, closing for now.
